One man was hit by lightning seven times, and survived every single one.
Roy Sullivan was a park ranger in Virginia.
In 1942, lightning hit his lookout tower. It burned a stripe down his leg, and blew off his big toenail.
In 1969, it hit him while he was driving his truck. It burned off his eyebrows.
A year later, it hit him in his own yard, and burned his shoulder.
In 1972, lightning hit him inside a ranger station, and set his hair on fire.
After that, he kept a bucket of water in his truck, just in case.
In 1973, it struck again. His hair caught fire, again.
In 1976, it hit him on patrol, and hurt his ankle.
And in 1977, it hit him while he was fishing. Then a bear tried to steal his fish. He hit it with a stick.
People started avoiding him during storms.
Today, he holds a world record. Seven lightning strikes, and two of his burned ranger hats are on display.
